Baseline site daily aggregated average energy consumption time series for Colorado The peak day, February 20, is shown in more detail in Figure 12, with 15-minute power data. Figure 12. Time series for peak day in Colorado before and after upgrade The baseline peak power was 12.9 kW per dwelling unit. After advanced air sealing with drill- and-fill wall insulation was applied to the dwelling units, the peak power decreased to 10.1 kW per dwelling unit, representing a 15.5% reduction. Notable savings occurred throughout the entire day, including early morning and late at night. The peaks and valleys generally maintained the same shape. 22 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4.3 Average Energy Bill Impact for Applicable Dwelling Units Only Energy bills for applicable units generally decreased after advanced air sealing with drill-and- fill wall insulation, as shown in Figure 13. Applicable dwelling units saw an average decrease in energy bills of 15%. The largest reduction in energy bills was for fuel oil, with an average savings of 38%, followed by natural gas at 26%, propane at 30%, and electricity at 9%. Figure 13.
